newsitem.title: USA: Rightist novel key evidence in McVeigh trial -TIME.
newsitem.headline: Rightist novel key evidence in McVeigh trial -TIME.

text.p: Prosecutors will use a photocopy of a passage from a white supremacist novel to try to establish the motive behind the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing, Time magazine reported on Sunday.
The photocopied passage was found in the alleged get-away car used by Timothy McVeigh, the prime suspect in the case who goes on trial in Denver next week, the magazine said.
The passage, found glued to an envelope containing papers, was taken from The Turner Diaries, a novel about right-wing extremists who blow up the FBI's headquarters in Washington.
The particular passage found in McVeigh's car explains that the bombing was necessary to wake up America.
The envelope was found when officials searched the car shortly after the April 19, 1995 bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal office building that killed 168 people.
Time, citing sources familiar with the envelope, said the prosecution will use the photocopied passage as key evidence to demonstrate the motive and the purpose of the bomb attack.
McVeigh, an embittered Gulf War veteran, has been linked to right-wing paramilitary militia groups opposed to the federal government.
He and co-defendant Terry Nichols are charged in the bombing and will be tried separately.
